correctness.rationale: A generator identity identifies each cyclic product with x0*x_sum and every minor preserves cyclic sum. The integral basis x0^(d-1)*xs is proven independent by the faithful degree-d image in Z[t,z]/(z^n-1). It proves all quantifiers and the chart Proj=Spec Z[z]/(z^n-1), including nilpotent structure. Frobenius factorization and simple roots for p∤m give exact local Artin lengths with no embedded contributions. Regularity and Hilbert-polynomial coefficient identity prove the supplementary all-characteristic Betti numbers. The packaged checker tests all quadratic minor incidence through n=8 and wild factorization cases; finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Primary statement is the explicit integral rank-one circulant projective group-scheme identification together with modular curvilinear degeneration for every n, including p|n. Generic rank-one determinantal results do not imply the scheme-theoretic nontransverse linear section. Pre-2016 generic circulant literature does address Cohen–Macaulayness/resolutions, which are acknowledged as prior; the fully readable arxiv:0809.1163 explicitly requires char not dividing n for its Fourier reduction, leaving the wild regime untreated in that account. Focused mathematical-record and published-literature comparisons found no covering theorem. Two close original articles remain partly inaccessible and could imply the result; this is recorded as a genuine risk rather than asserted noncoverage.
residual_risks: Original full text of Zaare-Nahandi (2002) could state equivalent integral group-scheme or modular-fiber conclusions; abstract alone cannot certify noncoverage.
Original full text of Zaare-Nahandi (2004) was unavailable. It proves nearby free-resolution statements and could include stronger invariant implications.

Generic circulant Cohen–Macaulayness, generic characteristic-prime-to-n Fourier diagonalization, and some Betti formulas are pre-existing results: only the proposed full wild-fiber scheme classification is assessed as new.

value.rationale: Bad-characteristic rank-one determinantal schemes are a natural boundary where the classical Fourier transformation degenerates. The complete integral flat family and m distinct curvilinear nonreduced components of length p^a give exact scheme structure, not merely a rank/dimension observation or a finite computation. This supplies a uniform local deformation benchmark for arbitrary modular circulant orders, separates geometric support from scheme length, and explains why generic-characteristic reduction arguments cannot be blindly specialized. The standard Betti invariance is contextual and not used alone to claim value.
